title.fr: Les Premières Nations, les Inuit et les Métis

text.en: Discover Canada uses the word “Indian” for those Aboriginal people who are neither Inuit nor Métis.
text.fr: Découvrir le Canada emploie le mot « Indien » pour désigner les personnes autochtones qui ne sont ni Inuit ni Métis.

source.quote: Indian refers to all Aboriginal people who are not Inuit or Métis.

verification.evidence: Today, the term Aboriginal peoples refers to three distinct groups: Indian refers to all Aboriginal people who are not Inuit or Métis.

text.en: The name First Nations came into use in the 1970s.
text.fr: L'expression « Premières Nations » est entrée dans l'usage dans les années 1970.

source.quote: In the 1970s, the term First Nations began to be used.

verification.evidence: In the 1970s, the term First Nations began to be used.

text.en: Many First Nations people have their homes on reserve land, in hundreds of communities. Others live off reserve, mostly in cities.
text.fr: Beaucoup de membres des Premières Nations ont leur foyer sur des terres de réserve, réparties en centaines de communautés. D'autres vivent hors réserve, surtout dans les villes.

source.quote: live on reserve land in about 600 communities while the other half live off-reserve, mainly in urban centres.

verification.evidence: Today, about half of First Nations people live on reserve land in about 600 communities while the other half live off-reserve, mainly in urban centres.

text.en: The Inuit live in small communities spread across the Arctic.
text.fr: Les Inuit vivent dans de petites communautés dispersées dans tout l'Arctique.

source.quote: live in small, scattered communities across the Arctic.

verification.evidence: The Inuit, which means “the people” in the Inuktitut language, live in small, scattered communities across the Arctic.

text.en: The Métis are a people of their own. Their ancestry is both Aboriginal and European.
text.fr: Les Métis forment un peuple distinct. Leurs origines sont à la fois autochtones et européennes.

source.quote: The Métis are a distinct people of mixed Aboriginal and European ancestry

verification.evidence: The Métis are a distinct people of mixed Aboriginal and European ancestry, the majority of whom live in the Prairie provinces.

text.en: The Métis have roots in French-speaking families and in English-speaking families alike.
text.fr: Les Métis ont des racines dans des familles francophones comme dans des familles anglophones.

source.quote: They come from both French- and English-speaking backgrounds

verification.evidence: The Métis are a distinct people of mixed Aboriginal and European ancestry, the majority of whom live in the Prairie provinces. They come from both French- and English-speaking backgrounds and speak their own dialect, Michif.
